clue.text: States of the Continental Divide? Just the opposite

definitions.text: States of the Continental Divide? Just the opposite

parts.words: States of the Continental Divide? Just the opposite
parts.note: the Continental Divide is a watershed splitting America; the opposite is a group of European states joined together rather than divided

explanation.surface: A geography teaser about the American watershed, turned on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue first suggests US states either side of the Rockies' Continental Divide; 'Just the opposite' asks for states of the Continent (Europe) that are united rather than divided.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloc is a political grouping of European countries, states of the Continent bound together.

clue.text: Newspaper creating uniform criterion

parts.note: making something uniform is evening it out
a criterion is a standard to judge by

explanation.surface: A newspaper that sets a single, uniform benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: The EVENING STANDARD is a London daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a long-running London daily paper.

clue.text: Old soldier put on fire engine from time to time?

definitions.text: Old soldier put on fire engine from time to time?

parts.words: Old soldier put on fire engine from time to time?
parts.note: an old British infantryman, named for his scarlet tunic, which is the same colour layer a fire engine gets when it is repainted

explanation.surface: A veteran trooper occasionally mounted on a fire appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: British soldiers of old wore scarlet tunics; a fire engine is periodically given a fresh layer of scarlet paint, so both 'wear' the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic British soldiers were nicknamed for their scarlet uniform jackets.

clue.text: An affair, naturally, that's routine

parts.note: an affair is a matter, a piece of business
naturally, as an interjection, means of course

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off an affair as only natural, all part of the routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regarded as normal and expected is done as routine.

clue.text: To the extent fashionable furniture's right

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
a sofa is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Trendy furniture is right, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to the degree that, limiting how far something applies.

clue.text: Perpetual harmony through total abstention from things like this?

definitions.text: Perpetual harmony through total abstention from things like this?

parts.words: Perpetual harmony through total abstention from things like this?
parts.note: a phrase for a relationship without quarrels; 'things like this' points at the puzzle itself, so it also means never once doing a puzzle of this kind

explanation.surface: A recipe for marital peace: give up the habit entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross word' is an angry remark; 'things like this' are crosswords, so swearing off them altogether also keeps the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who never quarrel are said to have had no angry exchange ever.

clue.text: Good objective set by monarch, male or female

parts.note: an objective is an end, a goal
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A good goal laid down by the sovereign, open to men or women.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical or social sex categories, masculine or feminine, are what the word names.

clue.text: Sticking with advantage he has before I have

parts.note: in tennis, advantage is shortened to ad
contracted, he has is he's
contracted, I have is I've

explanation.surface: Persisting while holding the edge, he claims priority over me.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue-like and tacky: an adjective for things that adhere.

clue.text: Measure of power one had in talk arranged with two

indicators.note: one letter is held within the rearranged letters, as a guest is had in a house
the letters of talk and two are set out in a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone joins a discussion, rearranged with a pair, to measure power.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a chat with two people; 'arranged' is the anagram signal for talk and two together (KLOWATT), and 'had in' sets the one letter inside it, after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand watts, a unit for rating electrical power.

clue.text: Provide a fine President of the US (but not now)

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

parts.words: President of the US (but not now)
parts.note: Gerald Ford was US President in the 1970s, a past holder of the office

explanation.surface: A small penalty is imposed by a former American leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply or offer something, as a view affords a vista.

clue.text: Girl that's cut short by military commander

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander

indicators.note: the word is docked of its final letter, cut short at the end

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A young woman is interrupted by an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the commander beside the shortened word; the 's of 'that's' is just 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, as in the detective novelist Christie.

clue.text: A very old and spiteful woman, one performing minor job

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful, catty woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: An ancient, malicious crone takes on a little task.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or sideline pursued besides one's main occupation.

clue.text: Ruddy good chap, not the Oxbridge type

parts.note: ruddy means reddish
a dependable, decent person is called a brick

explanation.surface: A rosy-cheeked decent fellow who did not go to an ancient university.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxbridge is Oxford and Cambridge; British universities founded later in industrial cities are called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Newer British universities, built of brick, contrast with the ancient stone colleges.

clue.text: Number ten in deadlock

explanation.surface: A prime minister at Downing Street stuck in an impasse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number ten' looks like Downing Street, but in rugby the fly-half wears 10.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the fly-half wears shirt 10 and has this other name; a stalemate between opponents is also so called.

clue.text: Followers of William, Greg and others

explanation.surface: Supporters of one man, like a golfer and his namesakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Greg Norman is an Australian golfer; William the Conqueror led the invaders of 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror's invading army came from Normandy; the golfer Greg shares the surname with others.

clue.text: Advance into stronghold, not recalled

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another, going into it

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
to advance is to go forward

explanation.surface: An attack pressed into a fortress was unremembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Failed to remember, the past tense of a lapse of memory.

clue.text: Curl of hair enclosed in covering letter

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the phrase that follows, enclosed in it

explanation.surface: A lock of hair tucked into a covering letter as a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spiral lock of hair.

clue.text: Female part in American Dream

indicators.note: only a portion of the words that follow is taken, part of the run

explanation.surface: A woman's role in a play about the American Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name.

clue.text: Instrument is initially measuring a living creature

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word is used, as it comes initially

explanation.surface: A gauge that first measures a living thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Any individual life form, plant or animal.

clue.text: Information about one kind of literature

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Background details on a type of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A category or style of artistic work, such as crime fiction.

clue.text: Unconcerned member of Parliamentary opposition?

explanation.surface: An offhand politician sitting on the opposition benches.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English Civil War the Royalists who fought Parliament were called by this name; 'Parliamentary opposition' suggests today's House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand and careless; also a Royalist who opposed the Roundhead Parliament.

clue.text: Hold as national hero

explanation.surface: Grip someone as a country's great figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Horatio Nelson, victor of Trafalgar, is Britain's naval hero; a wrestling hold has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip under the arms and behind the neck; also the admiral of Trafalgar.

clue.text: Impartial but not unconcerned, despite what some may think

definitions.text: Impartial but not unconcerned, despite what some may think

parts.words: Impartial but not unconcerned, despite what some may think
parts.note: a usage note: the word means neutral, having no stake, and many wrongly use it to mean bored or lacking interest

explanation.surface: A pedant's reminder about a commonly misused word.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue defines the word and corrects the frequent confusion with 'uninterested'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nothing to gain either way, hence neutral and fair.
